final.memo:
General Growth Properties is the nation’s second-largest mall owner, holding a portfolio of over 200 high-quality regional shopping centers [D01, D05]. These are dominant, asset-heavy businesses with significant barriers to entry that historically generate robust, stable cash flows [D01, D05].

This opportunity exists because the market has conflated a temporary liquidity crisis with a permanent impairment of value [D05]. Following a 99.1% share price collapse, the market currently prices the equity as a binary bankruptcy outcome with zero recovery [D04, D05]. We believe this narrative is fundamentally flawed, as the underlying NOI of the mall portfolio—exceeding $1.8 billion annually—significantly outweighs the debt burden if capital structure issues are resolved [D01, D02].

We are acquiring our position at an effective distressed option value relative to the underlying real estate [D04]. While we do not model growth in this scenario, a successful restructuring of the $27.767 billion in portfolio debt would allow the intrinsic value of the underlying assets to be reflected in the equity [D01, D02]. With a stabilized capital structure, we believe a multiple of 8x on core FFO provides an asymmetric return profile, with an expected IRR potential of 50% or more [D01, D02, D03].

Our role is that of a lead activist: we will move immediately to engage with lenders to negotiate a standstill and forbearance agreement for the $958 million in debt maturing December 1, 2008 [D03, D05]. We will press management to suspend non-core developments and preserve FFO for liquidity, ensuring we prevent a fire sale of the core assets [D01, D03, D05].

Risks remain high, primarily the potential for a total wipeout if creditors force an involuntary bankruptcy that bypasses common shareholders [D05]. We would change our mind if the $1.8 billion NOI run rate deteriorates or if management proves unable to negotiate maturity extensions [D01, D03, D05].

We are initiating a 5% target position. This is a high-risk, high-conviction activist turnaround that leverages our experience in real-estate-adjacent businesses to exploit a clear market mispricing [D08].
